content:
As Apple prepares to roll out its 2027 system versions, the WebKit blog has recently published a lengthy post detailing the new features of Safari 27.0. The following is a summary of the content.

The Safari MCP server is the most eye-catching new feature

Among the many new features of Safari 27.0, the most noteworthy is undoubtedly the Safari MCP server, which allows AI agents to control browser windows, helping developers boost their work efficiency.

To enable Safari MCP, developers need to go to "Safari > Settings > Developer" and check "Allow remote automation and external agents." Apple reminds users that the "Developer" panel will only appear after the user enables "Show features for web developers" under "Safari > Settings > Advanced."

Below is Apple's introduction to this new feature:

Are you using a coding agent to build websites? Safari 27.0 brings you the all-new Safari MCP server, making your workflow faster and more powerful. Let Claude Code, Codex, or your favourite agent take over the browser window and see how your code renders in real time. Safari MCP gives you access to the DOM, network requests, screenshots, and console output. Your agent can handle more work on its own, so you don't have to repeatedly switch windows, paste screenshots into the terminal, or keep typing prompts to explain what's going wrong. The Safari MCP server lets your agent: see how code renders in Safari; validate form, checkout flow, selection state, and other user states; compare computed styles and layouts with results from other browsers; test accessibility issues such as missing labels, incorrectly set ARIA properties, and insufficient contrast; analyse performance metrics such as load times and resource fetching times; and much more. The MCP server runs entirely locally, does not issue its own network requests, cannot access your personal data in Safari, and only sends the captured data to the agent you are using, not to Apple.

Apple's blog post also lists the specific commands developers need to use to connect Claude Code, Codex, or other agents to Safari, and welcomes developer feedback and feature suggestions.

In addition to MCP support, Safari 27.0 has also fixed nearly 850 issues, more than the 525 fixes Apple announced months ago at WWDC. The fixes span multiple areas including accessibility, CSS, encoding, fonts, forms, MathML, web, and WebRTC.

Safari 27.0 also adds support for immersive environments, allowing developers to deliver related experiences on visionOS, and extends the HTML <model> element to iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, enabling websites to embed interactive 3D models directly within pages in a way similar to images or videos.

The post also introduces the brand-new (and quite practical) "scroll anchoring" feature, which prevents the page from jumping when images load above the content the user is reading, and lists a number of Web Inspector improvements, including inline colour contrast information, a clearer view of redirect chains, and more powerful layout debugging capabilities.

The list also details improvements and new features across areas such as WebAssembly, WebGPU, JavaScript, CSS, WebRTC, media playback, Web Extensions, WKWebView, and Service Workers. The full article can be read here.
